transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Well, they told me I had to come see you because... my talking gets all mixed up, I guess. Like, I was just trying to explain to my boss about the keys for the supply closets. Heavy brass keys, you know? They clink together just like the ones down at the jail. I knew a guy in jail once who carved little birds out of soap, real detailed work... but anyway, I try to tell 'em about the keys, and the jail, and then the prayer rug I found. It had this pattern on it, all squares, and it made me think of my chess pieces. I always like playing the knights, they move different than the rest... but when I try to lay it all out for people, how the keys and the rug and the chess pieces all go together, they just stop me. They tell me they can't follow what I'm saying at all. So... I guess that's why I'm here.
Have you had a period of several days or more when you felt unusually high, energized, or much more irritable than usual?

Well, yeah, sometimes I get this... this feeling like I'm just on top of the world, you know? Like I'm ten feet tall and I got all this power just buzzing in my chest. I'll be laughing, talking real loud to everybody I see, feeling like the king of the castle. Which is funny, 'cause castles always have those big heavy doors with the iron hinges. I saw a documentary once about how they forged that iron, melting it down in these huge fires. Fire is something else, ain't it? The way it dances... but anyway, yeah, I feel real good, but then... if somebody looks at me wrong or asks me a stupid question, I just snap. I'll start shouting over nothing, just the littlest thing. Like the other day, this guy at the bus stop had his shoes tied wrong. Who ties their shoes with the loop underneath? It's just wrong. I used to have these boots with the metal hooks instead of holes, laced up real tight... but yeah, I get real mad, real fast if they question me when I'm feeling that good.
When you’re talking, do your thoughts ever seem to race so fast that you can’t keep up with them?

Oh, man, you have no idea. It's exactly like that. It feels like... like a whole crowd of people just talking and yelling inside my head all at the same time. They run so fast I can't even catch one before the next one hits me. I'll be trying to hold onto one idea, but it's already jumping from my light bill, over to the jail, then to the mosque, and then right into the cleaning chemicals I use on the night shift. 

We get these massive plastic jugs of the industrial floor stripper, you know? The yellow kind. You gotta be real careful with the yellow kind because it eats right through the wax if you let it sit. Waxing floors is an art, really. You gotta lay it down smooth with the mop in a figure-eight pattern. My uncle taught me that figure-eight motion when we used to go fishing, tying the line to the hook. We caught a catfish down at the creek once that was nearly as big as my leg, had whiskers on it like heavy wire... wire's getting real expensive now, you know. The copper thieves strip it right out of the walls at the empty office buildings I clean... 

But yeah, what were we talking about? The crowd in my head, right. It just jumps around from the bleach to the bills and the jail, just spinning faster than I can even get a word out.
Have you ever heard or seen things that other people could not?

Yeah... yeah, I do. It's usually when I'm working the night shift. Sometimes I hear this man's voice... it comes right out of the air vents, or sometimes from the mop closet when I'm mixing the chemicals. He calls my name, and then he tells me I ruined everything. It sounds so real, just like you're sitting right there talking to me. But the vents... you know, the ductwork in those old buildings is a real mess. The filters get all clogged up with dust and lint, sometimes even dead bugs. I used to catch bugs when I was a kid, put 'em in a glass jar with holes poked in the lid. You gotta poke the holes from the outside in, or the sharp edges will cut their little legs. I had this one beetle, shiny green, looked like a little jewel. My grandma had a brooch just like that color. She wore it to church every Sunday, pinned right on her collar... she always smelled like peppermint and mothballs. But yeah, the voice from the vent, it just tells me I ruined it all.
Have you ever had times when the voices or other unusual experiences were happening even when you were not feeling unusually energized or irritable?

Yeah... yeah, I know exactly what you mean. There have been these calmer weeks, you know? Times when I wasn't feeling all buzzed up and irritable, and I wasn't feeling all heavy and deeply depressed neither. Just... regular, just doing my job. But even then, for like more than two weeks straight, I was still hearing that man talking to me out of the vents. 

And I still believed all those office people in the building were signaling about me. Leaving their pens pointing at my cart, turning their coffee mugs a certain way to send messages to each other about me. They leave a lot of pens around, actually. Mostly those cheap blue ballpoints with the caps chewed up. I used to collect the ones they threw away, had a whole coffee can full of 'em at home. Old coffee cans are great for storing stuff, you know? Nails and screws and whatnot. My dad kept his whole garage organized with those metal Folgers cans. He drank it black, no sugar. He always said sugar was for hummingbirds. We had a hummingbird feeder on the front porch when I was little, this red plastic thing shaped like a flower. You gotta boil the sugar water just right or it goes bad in the sun... 

But yeah, what was the question? Oh, the voices. Yeah, even when my mood is totally fine and calm for a few weeks, I still hear the vent man and see the people signaling.
Have you ever had a stretch of at least one week when your mood was unusually elevated or irritable and your energy was much higher than usual?

Yeah... yeah, I have. Sometimes I get this... this feeling where I just feel so high up, you know? Like I'm powerful and I just got all this energy pumping through me. I'll be laughing and talking real loud to everybody, even the security guards at the building. I'll just be talking their ears off. But then, if one of 'em looks at me wrong or questions what I'm doing, I just snap. I'll start shouting over the smallest little thing. 

Like the other night, this guard, Frank... or maybe it was Dave, they all wear those same dark blue uniforms with the little silver badges. They buy those badges in bulk, I bet. You can get anything in bulk nowadays if you go to one of those big warehouse stores. My sister used to have a membership to one of those places. She'd buy giant jars of mayonnaise, like, gallon-sized jars. Who eats that much mayonnaise? Unless you're making a whole lot of potato salad for a church picnic or something. I love potato salad, but you gotta put a little mustard in it to give it a kick. Not too much, just a dab. My mom used to use that spicy brown mustard, the kind with the little seeds in it. 

But yeah, I'll be feeling all powerful and loud, and then I just explode if somebody questions me. It lasts for a week or more sometimes, just like that.
Have there been times when you were hearing the voice or feeling that people were signaling about you even when you were not having any mood episode at all?

Yeah... yeah, I think I already mentioned that, but yeah. There have definitely been these calmer stretches... times when I wasn't feeling all buzzed up and powerful, and I wasn't feeling completely down in the dumps either. Just completely normal, regular mood. But even during those times, for like more than two weeks straight, I was still hearing that man talking to me from the vents. And I still knew the office workers were leaving those signals with their pens and mugs. 

I guess they drink a lot of coffee up there on the fifth floor. It's an accounting firm, I think. Lots of numbers, lots of paper. They have these huge recycling bins, the blue ones, and they're always overflowing with shredded paper. It looks like snow when you dump it into the main dumpster out back. I used to love the snow when I was a kid. We'd build these giant forts in the front yard and stockpile snowballs. You gotta pack 'em tight so they don't fall apart when you throw 'em. My brother got hit right in the ear with an iceball once... cried for an hour. My mom had to put a warm washcloth on it. She always used those thin white washcloths with the little pink stripes on the edges. They sell those in packs of ten at the dollar store now, but back then they seemed so fancy... 

But anyway, yeah, even when my mood is totally fine for a few weeks, the vent man and the signals are still there.
Have you ever had at least two weeks when the voices or beliefs like people were sending you messages were present even though your mood was completely normal?

Yeah, doctor, I... I think we just went over this, didn't we? But yeah, I know what you're asking. There are definitely those calmer weeks. Times when I'm not feeling all high and mighty, and I'm not feeling all heavy and sad either. Just regular. But even then, for like, well over two weeks straight, I still hear that man talking to me from the vents. And I still know those office people are leaving those signals for each other about me. 

They really do leave a lot of stuff around, you know? Not just the pens. Sometimes it's paperclips. The big silver ones, not the little ones. The little ones are useless, they just bend if you try to clip more than three pieces of paper together. I don't know why they even make the little ones anymore. It's a waste of metal. Metal's expensive nowadays. You see guys driving around in pickup trucks on trash day, looking for scrap metal. Old washing machines, busted lawnmowers, anything they can take to the scrapyard for a few bucks. My uncle used to do that. He had this beat-up old Ford Ranger, rust all over the wheel wells. The tailgate wouldn't even latch right, he had to tie it shut with a piece of yellow nylon rope. Nylon rope is strong, but it frays at the ends if you don't burn it with a lighter. You gotta melt the tips just right or it unravels like a bad sweater. My grandma used to knit these awful itchy sweaters for us every Christmas... 

But yeah, like I was saying, even when my mood is completely normal for a couple weeks, the vent man is still talking and the signals are still happening. It doesn't stop just 'cause I'm feeling okay.
During those times when your mood was high and your energy was up, did you also need much less sleep than usual?

Yeah, sleep just... it just goes out the window. I can sleep two or three hours, tops, and I get up before dawn feeling completely fresh. It's like sleep is something other people need, not me. I just start planning out all my work, getting everything lined up. 

I actually like being up before dawn, you know? It's real quiet. The streets are empty, except for the street sweepers. Have you ever watched one of those street sweepers go by? They have those huge brushes that spin around, throwing all the dirt and leaves up into the belly of the truck. I always wondered how often they have to replace those brushes. They must wear down pretty fast, scraping against the asphalt all night. Asphalt is tough stuff. They paved my street last summer, and the smell of the hot tar was just everywhere. It sticks to your shoes, too. You gotta be careful not to track it into the house, or it ruins the carpet. My landlord put this cheap beige carpet in my apartment. Who puts beige carpet in a rental? It shows every single stain. You spill one drop of coffee, and it's there forever. I tried using that foaming carpet cleaner on it once, the kind in the aerosol can with the little plastic scrubber on top. You spray it on and let it sit for five minutes, but it never really gets the stain out. It just smells like fake lemons and disappointment. 

But yeah, when I'm feeling that high, I don't need sleep at all. Just a couple hours and I'm ready to go.
Have you ever had times when the voices or beliefs like people were sending you messages were present even when your mood was completely normal?

Doc, are you... are you feeling alright? Because I swear you just asked me this exact same thing a few minutes ago. We keep going in circles here. But yeah, I'll say it again. There have definitely been calmer weeks where I wasn't especially high, and I wasn't deeply depressed either. Just totally normal. But even then, for more than two weeks at a time, I still heard the man in the vents, and I still believed the people in the building were signaling about me. 

Speaking of circles, they have this big glass revolving door down in the main lobby of the building. I absolutely hate cleaning the glass on that thing. People are supposed to push the metal bar, right? That's what it's there for. But they don't. They put their bare hands right on the glass and leave these big oily handprints. Kids are the absolute worst for it. They just smear their sticky little fingers everywhere. I don't even know what kids eat nowadays to get their hands so sticky all the time. Probably those gummy fruit snacks. My sister used to buy those huge bulk boxes of them for her kids. They're shaped like little dinosaurs or sharks or something, but they just taste like wax and cherry syrup. You gotta watch out for that red dye, too. Red dye number 40. I saw a show on public television that said it makes kids bounce off the walls. I like watching public television late at night. They have those old British shows where everyone lives in a big manor house and drinks tea. They always have very nice teacups, the kind with the little matching saucers... 

But, anyway, yeah. My mood can be totally normal for a couple weeks, but the vent guy and the signals are still happening.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you felt very depressed or lost interest in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah, I definitely get those... those really bad spells. On my bad days, I just sit on the edge of the bed after my morning prayer, and I feel so heavy. Just empty inside. Like there's no point in even cleaning myself up or going outside. 

It's hard to explain that heaviness. It feels like you're wearing wet clothes. Have you ever been caught in a really sudden downpour? We had one of those last spring. I was walking back from the corner store with a gallon of milk, and the sky just opened up. Completely soaked me to the bone in seconds. The plastic bag broke, too. They make those bags so thin now. You try to carry anything heavier than a loaf of bread and the handles just stretch right out until they snap. I miss the old paper bags. They had that nice thick brown paper. You could use them to cover your textbooks in school. We used to do that back in junior high. We'd fold the paper bags over the covers and draw all over them with ballpoint pens. I used to draw cars. Big muscle cars with flames on the side. I wanted a Camaro so bad back then. A 1969 Camaro RS, cherry red with the white racing stripes. My buddy Jimmy's older brother had one, and he'd let us sit in it sometimes if we promised not to touch the radio. The radio had these little silver knobs that clicked when you turned them. You don't see knobs like that anymore, everything is all digital and touch screens now. You tap the screen and half the time it doesn't even register your finger. My phone does that. I have to tap the screen three times just to answer a call...

But yeah, the depression. It gets really bad for weeks at a time. I just sit there feeling completely empty, like nothing matters.
Have you ever had a period of at least one week when you felt so unusually energized or high that you got into trouble or your behavior was very out of character for you?

Yeah, I get like that. Sometimes I just feel so... so powerful, you know? Like I'm on top of the world. I'll be laughing, talking real loud to everybody in the building, just feeling completely unstoppable. But then, if somebody looks at me wrong or questions what I'm doing, I can just snap. I'll start shouting over the smallest little thing. 

Like this one time, this guy on the third floor asked me why I was mopping the hallway twice. I just lost it on him. I told him he didn't know the first thing about floor maintenance. Floor maintenance is a real art, you know? You have to use the right ratio of cleaner to water. If you use too much soap, it leaves a film. A sticky film that catches all the dust and dirt from people's shoes. And people wear the worst shoes for floors. Those heavy work boots with the deep treads? They track in mud, salt in the winter... rock salt is terrible for linoleum. It scratches the finish right off. You have to strip it and re-wax it, and that takes hours. You need one of those big rotary floor buffers. The ones that weigh like a hundred pounds. You have to swing it side to side, from your hips. It's a real workout. My buddy used to work at a bowling alley, and he said buffing the lanes was even harder. They use this special oil on bowling lanes. Did you know that? They oil the lanes so the ball hooks right. I used to bowl in a league on Thursday nights. We had these matching shirts, bright green with our names embroidered on the pocket. My name was stitched in this yellow thread that started unraveling after three washes. You can't find good embroidery anymore. Everything is just screen-printed now, and the print cracks and peels off in the dryer...

But yeah, I get really energized and loud, and if somebody gets in my way, I just explode on them. It definitely gets me into trouble.
Have there been any times when the voices or beliefs were present only during your mood episodes and completely went away when your mood was back to normal?

Well, no, it's not like they completely go away when my mood is normal. I told you, I still hear the guy in the vents even on my calm weeks. But... yeah, when my mood is all over the place, the voices and the signals are definitely there too. Like, when I get into those states where I'm only sleeping a couple of hours a night and I'm drawing up all these big master plans to completely reorganize the building's maintenance schedule... during those times, the vent voice is right there with me, and I feel absolutely sure the hallway lights flickering are sending out warnings about me. 

Speaking of the hallway lights, they use these cheap fluorescent tubes now. The ballasts go bad all the time, and they just hum. It's this low, constant buzzing sound that drives you crazy if you stand under it too long. And they give off this awful greenish light that makes everybody look sick. I remember when buildings used to have real incandescent bulbs. They had that warm, yellow glow. Made things look cozy. My grandmother had this big floor lamp in her living room with a fringed shade. It was real heavy, made of brass, I think. She kept it right next to her reading chair. She used to read these thick romance novels, the ones with the painted covers where the guy always has his shirt ripped open. She'd get them by the dozen from the used bookstore downtown. That bookstore smelled like old paper and dust. They had a cat that just slept on the counter all day. A big orange tabby. I had an orange cat once, named Marmalade. He used to bring dead mice and leave them right on the welcome mat. You'd step out in the morning and nearly squish them. Mice are a huge problem in older buildings, you know. They get into the walls and chew through the wiring. That's a huge fire hazard. You have to put down traps, but the snap traps are messy, and the glue traps just seem cruel...

But yeah, when I'm all wired and making those big plans, the vent guy and the light warnings are definitely happening at the same time.
Have you ever had hallucinations or delusional beliefs when you were not having a mood episode, such as a manic or depressive episode?

Yeah, definitely. Like I was saying before, there are plenty of times when I'm just... regular. You know? Not stuck in bed feeling depressed, and not all fired up and yelling at people. Just a normal, calm mood. But even during those calm stretches, for like two or three weeks at a time, I still hear the man in the vents plain as day. And I still know people in the building are signaling about me. 

It's especially loud when I'm working near the main intake grates in the hallways. Those grates are massive. You wouldn't believe the amount of dust that gets sucked into those things. Management is supposed to order the good pleated filters, the thick ones, but they always cheap out and buy those flimsy blue fiberglass ones. They don't catch a damn thing. All the dust just blows right through the system and settles right back down on the baseboards. I swear I spend half my life wiping down baseboards. You can't just use a dry duster, either, or it just kicks the dirt right back into the air. You gotta use a damp rag. We used to use old cut-up t-shirts for rags when I was growing up. My mom kept a whole drawer of them under the kitchen counter. That drawer always got stuck in the summer when it was humid. The wood swells up, you know? You have to take a bar of soap and rub it along the wooden runners to make it glide smooth again. Plain old bar soap. Ivory works the best for that. Did you know Ivory soap floats? I dropped a bar in the bathtub when I was maybe eight years old, and it just bobbed right there on the top of the water. We only got to take real baths on Sunday nights before the school week started. You had to make sure you scrubbed behind your ears, or the teacher would send you to the nurse's office to get checked for lice...
Have the voices or beliefs ever continued for at least two weeks when you were not having any manic or depressive symptoms at all?

Yeah, like I was just saying, I have those calm stretches. I'll have those calmer weeks where I'm not especially high or deeply depressed, just... regular, you know? But yeah, it's definitely been for more than two weeks at a time during those calm periods where I still hear the man in the vents every single day, and I still know the people in the building are signaling about me. It doesn't just go away because my mood is normal. 

Two weeks is a long time to deal with that. Actually, two weeks is exactly how long management made us wait for a new fan belt for the rooftop AC unit last August. Two whole weeks! You wouldn't believe how hot the top floor gets when the air goes out. It's like an oven up there. The tenants were complaining to me non-stop, leaving sticky notes on my utility cart. They think I can just magically fix it, but I don't carry commercial fan belts in my back pocket. You have to order those from a specialty supply house. 

And the supply houses aren't like they used to be, let me tell you. Used to be you could just drive down to the industrial park on 4th street and pick up whatever you needed. There was this guy there, Sal, who knew every part number by heart. He didn't even need to look at a computer. Computers ruin everything, if you ask me. Everything is automated now. You call a number and get a robot voice telling you to press one for sales, press two for service. My sister got locked out of her bank account last month because she couldn't get past the robot on the phone. She just wanted to check her balance, but it kept asking her for a PIN she forgot. She had to drive all the way down to the physical branch, and the parking there is an absolute nightmare. They have those tiny spots that barely fit a compact car, let alone her big station wagon. It's a real boat of a car, one of those old ones with the fake wood paneling on the side. You don't see cars like that anymore. Now they all look like jellybeans. Just round and silver or white. Nobody buys a green or a blue car anymore... 

But yeah, even when my mood is totally fine for over two weeks, the vent guy is still talking and the signals are still happening.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you heard voices or believed people were sending you messages while you were not having any manic or depressive symptoms at all?

Didn't we... I think I just said that, didn't I? But yeah, yes. Like I was telling you, there have been those calmer weeks. Times when I'm not especially high, and I'm not deeply depressed, just... regular. But even then, for more than two weeks straight, I still hear the man in the vents, and I still know the people in the building are signaling about me. It doesn't stop just 'cause my mood is fine. 

Two weeks... you know, speaking of two weeks, that's usually how long you have to wait to get any kind of doctor's appointment anywhere these days anyway. Actually, it's worse now. I tried to get in to see the dentist last month because my lower bridge was aching. Just a dull throb, right where the gum meets the metal. The receptionist—she had this bright purple hair, like, unnatural purple, like grape soda—she told me they couldn't see me until November. November! Who can wait that long with a toothache? I ended up just swishing warm salt water. Salt water fixes a lot of things. My granddad used to swear by it. He lived on the coast, out in Maine. Had this little dinghy he'd take out to check lobster traps. He smelled like brine and old tobacco. He used to smoke a pipe, the kind with a curved stem, always tapping it out on the heel of his boot... they don't make boots like they used to, either. Now the soles just peel right off if you step in a puddle.
Have the voices or beliefs ever been present only when you were feeling unusually high or irritable, and not at other times?

Doc, are you pulling my leg? I feel like a broken record here. No, it's not just when I'm high or irritable. Like I keep trying to tell you, there have been those calmer weeks where I'm not especially high, and I'm not deeply depressed either. Just regular. But even then, for more than two weeks at a stretch, I still hear the man in the vents, and I still believe the people in the building are signaling about me. It doesn't only happen when my mood is all over the place. 

I really do feel like a broken record, though. You know, actual records are making a big comeback. I had to clear out apartment 4B a couple months ago after the tenant passed away, and his kids didn't want to deal with his stuff. Just left everything for me to deal with. He had all these plastic milk crates full of old vinyl records. Heavy as lead, let me tell you. I had to haul every single one of them down to the dumpster by myself. My lower back was screaming by the end of the shift. I tried going to one of those chiropractors once for my back, the guys that crack your neck? Scared the living daylights out of me. Sounded like a dry branch snapping in half. I prefer just using a heating pad now. I got one of those electric ones with the auto-shutoff timer, which is a lifesaver because I always fall asleep with it turned on. You really don't want to start a fire in the bed. Mattresses are basically kindling these days with all that memory foam stuff. It's just solid chemicals. Smells weird when you first take it out of the plastic wrapper, too. Like a chemical factory. You have to leave the windows open for days just to air the room out...
Have there ever been at least two weeks when you had the voices or beliefs like people were sending you messages, but you were not having any mood symptoms at all?

Are you... wait, are you messing with me? Is this a test? Because I swear I've answered this exact same question like three times already. But yeah, yes, I'll say it again. There are those calmer weeks, right? Times when I'm not high, and I'm not deeply depressed. Just regular. But even then, for more than two weeks, I still hear the man in the vents, and I still know the people in the building are signaling about me. 

It's like talking to a brick wall here, Doc. Speaking of brick walls, the masonry on the east side of the building is starting to crumble. I noticed it last Tuesday when I was hosing down the sidewalk. The mortar is just turning to sand. I told the property manager, Mr. Henderson, but he just waved me off. He's always waving me off. He wears these cheap suits that look like they're made out of shiny plastic, and he always has a golf club in his office. Who plays golf in an office? It's ridiculous. He's got one of those little putting greens on the carpet. Carpet in an office is a terrible idea anyway. It just traps all the dirt and the coffee spills. You can never really get a coffee stain out of a light-colored carpet, no matter how much of that foaming spray you use. I've tried everything. Baking soda, vinegar, club soda... club soda works okay on blood, actually, if you get to it fast enough. Not that I clean up a lot of blood, but sometimes a tenant will cut their finger on a broken glass in the trash chute. People just throw loose glass down the chute! It's incredibly dangerous. I have to wear these thick leather gloves when I change the bins, the kind welders wear. They're stiff and you can barely bend your fingers, but it's better than getting sliced open. My buddy Tom got sliced open once, had to get twelve stitches...
Have there been any periods when the hallucinations or beliefs were present only during times you were depressed or manic, and not at other times?

Doc, are we doing some kind of memory test? Because I'm starting to think you're the one who needs a checkup. I just... I literally just told you this. No, it's not only when I'm depressed or manic. I've had those calmer weeks, right? Weeks where I'm not high as a kite and I'm not down in the dumps. Just completely regular. But even then, for over two weeks, I still hear the man in the vents, and I still know for a fact the people in the building are signaling about me. It doesn't just happen when my mood is off. 

Speaking of off, the thermostat in the lobby is completely shot. I've been telling Henderson for a month that it's stuck on 78 degrees. It's like a sauna down there. The poor ferns by the front desk are turning brown at the tips. You really have to mist ferns, you know? They like humidity, but not baking heat. My aunt had this massive Boston fern hanging on her porch. Thing was the size of a Volkswagen. She used to water it with leftover tea. Said the tannins were good for the soil. She drank a lot of tea, mostly that Earl Grey stuff. Smells like perfume to me. I prefer coffee. Black, no sugar. Sugar just rots your teeth anyway, which brings me right back to my lower bridge aching. I still haven't heard back from that purple-haired receptionist. You'd think she could at least put me on a cancellation list. People cancel dentist appointments all the time. Nobody actually wants to go to the dentist. They just go because they have to, like getting your car inspected. Speaking of cars, my registration is due next month, and the lines at the DMV... don't even get me started. You have to take a number and just sit there on those hard plastic chairs for hours. They always play the most depressing daytime TV on those little screens in the corner, too...
Have these voices or beliefs been going on, overall, for at least six months?

Yeah, yeah, it's been way longer than six months. The voices and all that stuff with the people in the building... it's been going on for about a year and a half now. Ever since the winter before last. 

Man, that was a brutal winter, too. The pipes in the basement froze solid twice in one week. I was down there with a blowtorch and a space heater for hours trying to thaw them out before they burst. You ever see a cast iron pipe burst? It's like a bomb going off. Water everywhere, ruins everything. And the smell of stagnant water in a basement... it never really goes away. It gets into the concrete. You have to scrub it down with bleach, but then the whole building smells like a swimming pool for a month. I used to swim a lot when I was a kid. We had this public pool in my neighborhood, cost fifty cents to get in for the whole day. They had this high dive that felt like it was a hundred feet tall. I only jumped off it once, belly flopped so hard I thought I ruptured something. My chest was red for a week. I don't think they even build high dives at public pools anymore, too much liability. Everyone's so worried about getting sued these days. You can't even mop a floor without putting up six of those yellow caution signs, or someone will slip on purpose just to get a payout. I saw a guy do it once in the lobby, literally laid down on the wet tile and started groaning. I told Henderson to check the security tapes...

We get these massive plastic jugs of the industrial floor stripper, you know? The yellow kind. You gotta be real careful with the yellow kind because it eats right through the wax if you let it sit. Waxing floors is an art, really. You gotta lay it down smooth with the mop in a figure-eight pattern. You try to carry anything heavier than a loaf of bread and the handles just stretch right out until they snap. I miss the old paper bags. They had that nice thick brown paper. You could use them to cover your textbooks in school. We used to do that back in junior high. We'd fold the paper bags over the covers and draw all over them with ballpoint pens. I used to draw cars. Big muscle cars with flames on the side. I wanted a Camaro so bad back then. A 1969 Camaro RS, cherry red with the white racing stripes. My buddy Jimmy's older brother had one, and he'd let us sit in it sometimes if we promised not to touch the radio. The radio had these little silver knobs that clicked when you turned them. You don't see knobs like that anymore, everything is all digital and touch screens now. You tap the screen and half the time it doesn't even register your finger. My phone does that. My buddy used to work at a bowling alley, and he said buffing the lanes was even harder. They use this special oil on bowling lanes. Did you know that? They oil the lanes so the ball hooks right. I used to bowl in a league on Thursday nights. We had these matching shirts, bright green with our names embroidered on the pocket. They get into the walls and chew through the wiring. That's a huge fire hazard. You have to put down traps, but the snap traps are messy, and the glue traps just seem cruel...

Two weeks is a long time to deal with that. Actually, two weeks is exactly how long management made us wait for a new fan belt for the rooftop AC unit last August. Two whole weeks! You wouldn't believe how hot the top floor gets when the air goes out. It's like an oven up there. The tenants were complaining to me non-stop, leaving sticky notes on my utility cart. They think I can just magically fix it, but I don't carry commercial fan belts in my back pocket. You have to order those from a specialty supply house. 

And the supply houses aren't like they used to be, let me tell you. Used to be you could just drive down to the industrial park on 4th street and pick up whatever you needed. There was this guy there, Sal, who knew every part number by heart. He didn't even need to look at a computer. Computers ruin everything, if you ask me. Everything is automated now. You call a number and get a robot voice telling you to press one for sales, press two for service. My sister got locked out of her bank account last month because she couldn't get past the robot on the phone. She just wanted to check her balance, but it kept asking her for a PIN she forgot. She had to drive all the way down to the physical branch, and the parking there is an absolute nightmare. They have those tiny spots that barely fit a compact car, let alone her big station wagon. It's a real boat of a car, one of those old ones with the fake wood paneling on the side. You don't see cars like that anymore. Now they all look like jellybeans. Just round and silver or white. Nobody buys a green or a blue car anymore... 

But yeah, even when my mood is totally fine for over two weeks, the vent guy is still talking and the signals are still happening.

doctor.question: Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you heard voices or believed people were sending you messages while you were not having any manic or depressive symptoms at all?

patient.answer:
Didn't we... I think I just said that, didn't I? But yeah, yes. Like I was telling you, there have been those calmer weeks. Times when I'm not especially high, and I'm not deeply depressed, just... regular. But even then, for more than two weeks straight, I still hear the man in the vents, and I still know the people in the building are signaling about me. It doesn't stop just 'cause my mood is fine. 

Two weeks... you know, speaking of two weeks, that's usually how long you have to wait to get any kind of doctor's appointment anywhere these days anyway. Actually, it's worse now. I tried to get in to see the dentist last month because my lower bridge was aching. Just a dull throb, right where the gum meets the metal. The receptionist—she had this bright purple hair, like, unnatural purple, like grape soda—she told me they couldn't see me until November. November! Who can wait that long with a toothache? I ended up just swishing warm salt water. Salt water fixes a lot of things. My granddad used to swear by it. He lived on the coast, out in Maine. Had this little dinghy he'd take out to check lobster traps. He smelled like brine and old tobacco. He used to smoke a pipe, the kind with a curved stem, always tapping it out on the heel of his boot... they don't make boots like they used to, either. Now the soles just peel right off if you step in a puddle.

doctor.intent: Clarify whether there is a history of psychotic symptoms occurring only during times of mood elevation, which would help distinguish schizoaffective disorder from schizophrenia.
doctor.question: Have the voices or beliefs ever been present only when you were feeling unusually high or irritable, and not at other times?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 3
target_item.manifestation: There have been calmer weeks when I was not especially high or deeply depressed, but for more than two weeks I still heard the man in the vents and believed people in the building were signaling about me.
target_item.reason: The doctor is again asking about the timing of the psychotic symptoms in relation to mood episodes, specifically whether they only occur during manic episodes or if they occur independently. This directly relates to the requirement of having delusions/hallucinations in the absence of a major mood episode.

patient.answer:
Doc, are you pulling my leg? I feel like a broken record here. No, it's not just when I'm high or irritable. Like I keep trying to tell you, there have been those calmer weeks where I'm not especially high, and I'm not deeply depressed either. Just regular. But even then, for more than two weeks at a stretch, I still hear the man in the vents, and I still believe the people in the building are signaling about me. It doesn't only happen when my mood is all over the place. 

I really do feel like a broken record, though. You know, actual records are making a big comeback. I had to clear out apartment 4B a couple months ago after the tenant passed away, and his kids didn't want to deal with his stuff. Just left everything for me to deal with. He had all these plastic milk crates full of old vinyl records. Heavy as lead, let me tell you. I had to haul every single one of them down to the dumpster by myself. My lower back was screaming by the end of the shift. I tried going to one of those chiropractors once for my back, the guys that crack your neck? Scared the living daylights out of me. Sounded like a dry branch snapping in half. I prefer just using a heating pad now. I got one of those electric ones with the auto-shutoff timer, which is a lifesaver because I always fall asleep with it turned on. You really don't want to start a fire in the bed. Mattresses are basically kindling these days with all that memory foam stuff. It's just solid chemicals. Smells weird when you first take it out of the plastic wrapper, too. Like a chemical factory. You have to leave the windows open for days just to air the room out...

doctor.intent: Determine whether there has been a distinct period of psychotic symptoms lasting at least 2 weeks in the absence of mood symptoms, which would favor schizoaffective disorder over bipolar disorder with psychotic features.
doctor.question: Have there ever been at least two weeks when you had the voices or beliefs like people were sending you messages, but you were not having any mood symptoms at all?

target_item.reason: The doctor is again asking if the psychotic symptoms (voices and beliefs) have occurred for at least two weeks without any mood symptoms, which directly maps to Additional Requirement 3.

patient.answer:
Are you... wait, are you messing with me? Is this a test? Because I swear I've answered this exact same question like three times already. But yeah, yes, I'll say it again. There are those calmer weeks, right? Times when I'm not high, and I'm not deeply depressed. Just regular. But even then, for more than two weeks, I still hear the man in the vents, and I still know the people in the building are signaling about me. 

It's like talking to a brick wall here, Doc. Speaking of brick walls, the masonry on the east side of the building is starting to crumble. I noticed it last Tuesday when I was hosing down the sidewalk. The mortar is just turning to sand. I told the property manager, Mr. Henderson, but he just waved me off. He's always waving me off. He wears these cheap suits that look like they're made out of shiny plastic, and he always has a golf club in his office. Who plays golf in an office? It's ridiculous. He's got one of those little putting greens on the carpet. Carpet in an office is a terrible idea anyway. It just traps all the dirt and the coffee spills. You can never really get a coffee stain out of a light-colored carpet, no matter how much of that foaming spray you use. I've tried everything. Baking soda, vinegar, club soda... club soda works okay on blood, actually, if you get to it fast enough. Not that I clean up a lot of blood, but sometimes a tenant will cut their finger on a broken glass in the trash chute. People just throw loose glass down the chute! It's incredibly dangerous. I have to wear these thick leather gloves when I change the bins, the kind welders wear. They're stiff and you can barely bend your fingers, but it's better than getting sliced open. My buddy Tom got sliced open once, had to get twelve stitches...

doctor.intent: Determine whether psychotic symptoms occur exclusively during mood episodes, which distinguishes schizoaffective disorder from schizophrenia.
doctor.question: Have there been any periods when the hallucinations or beliefs were present only during times you were depressed or manic, and not at other times?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 3

patient.answer:
Doc, are we doing some kind of memory test? Because I'm starting to think you're the one who needs a checkup. I just... I literally just told you this. No, it's not only when I'm depressed or manic. I've had those calmer weeks, right? Weeks where I'm not high as a kite and I'm not down in the dumps. Just completely regular. But even then, for over two weeks, I still hear the man in the vents, and I still know for a fact the people in the building are signaling about me. It doesn't just happen when my mood is off. 

Speaking of off, the thermostat in the lobby is completely shot. I've been telling Henderson for a month that it's stuck on 78 degrees. It's like a sauna down there. The poor ferns by the front desk are turning brown at the tips. You really have to mist ferns, you know? They like humidity, but not baking heat. My aunt had this massive Boston fern hanging on her porch. Thing was the size of a Volkswagen. She used to water it with leftover tea. Said the tannins were good for the soil. She drank a lot of tea, mostly that Earl Grey stuff. Smells like perfume to me. I prefer coffee. Black, no sugar. Sugar just rots your teeth anyway, which brings me right back to my lower bridge aching. I still haven't heard back from that purple-haired receptionist. You'd think she could at least put me on a cancellation list. People cancel dentist appointments all the time. Nobody actually wants to go to the dentist. They just go because they have to, like getting your car inspected. Speaking of cars, my registration is due next month, and the lines at the DMV... don't even get me started. You have to take a number and just sit there on those hard plastic chairs for hours. They always play the most depressing daytime TV on those little screens in the corner, too...

doctor.intent: Determine whether the psychotic symptoms persist for at least 6 months overall, which would favor schizophrenia over schizoaffective disorder or bipolar disorder with psychotic features.
doctor.question: Have these voices or beliefs been going on, overall, for at least six months?

target_item.name: Psychotic Symptoms Duration
target_item.manifestation: The voices and fixed worries about being watched or marked have been with me for about a year and a half.

patient.answer:
Yeah, yeah, it's been way longer than six months. The voices and all that stuff with the people in the building... it's been going on for about a year and a half now. Ever since the winter before last. 

Man, that was a brutal winter, too. The pipes in the basement froze solid twice in one week. I was down there with a blowtorch and a space heater for hours trying to thaw them out before they burst. You ever see a cast iron pipe burst? It's like a bomb going off. Water everywhere, ruins everything. And the smell of stagnant water in a basement... it never really goes away. It gets into the concrete. You have to scrub it down with bleach, but then the whole building smells like a swimming pool for a month. I used to swim a lot when I was a kid. We had this public pool in my neighborhood, cost fifty cents to get in for the whole day. They had this high dive that felt like it was a hundred feet tall. I only jumped off it once, belly flopped so hard I thought I ruptured something. My chest was red for a week. I don't think they even build high dives at public pools anymore, too much liability. Everyone's so worried about getting sued these days. You can't even mop a floor without putting up six of those yellow caution signs, or someone will slip on purpose just to get a payout. I saw a guy do it once in the lobby, literally laid down on the wet tile and started groaning. I told Henderson to check the security tapes...

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a clear manic syndrome (elevated/irritable mood, decreased need for sleep, pressured/excessive talking, racing thoughts, increased energy, behavioral outbursts) plus prominent psychotic symptoms (auditory hallucinations and persecutory ideas). Psychotic symptoms persist for more than 2 weeks during euthymic periods, establishing schizoaffective disorder rather than a mood disorder with psychotic features. Because the manic episodes are prominent and no sustained depressive syndrome is required for the diagnosis, the best fit is schizoaffective disorder, manic type (F25.0), rather than bipolar disorder with psychotic symptoms or paranoid schizophrenia.
